{{short description|American biologist}}
'''Joshua S. Weitz''' is an American biologist. He is both a professor of biology and the Clark Leadership Chair in Data Analytics at the [[University of Maryland]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Leslie |title=Joshua Weitz Joins Biology as Professor and Clark Leadership Chair in Data Analytics |url=https://biology.umd.edu/news/please-join-us-welcome-dr-joshua-weitz |website=News |publisher=University of Maryland |access-date=12 September 2023 |date=5 July 2023}}</ref> Previously, he was a professor at [[Georgia Tech]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://biosci.gatech.edu/people/joshua-weitz |title=Joshua Weitz |publisher=gatech.edu |accessdate=December 22, 2017}}</ref> where he was the founding director of the Interdisciplinary Graduate Program in Quantitative Biosciences.<ref>{{cite web |title=Director Joshua Weitz welcomes the inaugural class to the QBioS Ph.D. at Georgia Tech |url=http://qbios.gatech.edu/director%E2%80%99s-welcome |date=August 31, 2016 |accessdate=September 10, 2018}}</ref>  In 2017, he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://cos.gatech.edu/hg/item/598901 |title=Joshua Weitz Elected AAAS Fellow |date=November 21, 2017 |publisher=gatech.edu |accessdate=September 10, 2018}}</ref>

==Education==
He earned his A.B at [[Princeton University]] in 1997 and his Ph.D. in physics at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 2003.<ref name="GATECH">{{Cite web |url=http://ecotheory.biology.gatech.edu/people/joshua-weitz |title=Joshua Weitz |publisher=gatech.edu |accessdate=December 22, 2017}}</ref>

==Research==
Weitz's interests are the dynamics and structure of complex biology systems.<ref name="GATECH"/> In particular, Joshua Weitz's research focuses on the quantitative evaluation of virus-host interactions. The quantitative edge that he brought to the field is summarized in the award winning book ''Quantitative Viral Ecology'',<ref>{{cite book |last1=Weitz |first1=Joshua |title=Quantitative Viral Ecology: Dynamics of Viruses and Their Microbial Hosts |date=January 5, 2016 |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=978-0691161549}}</ref> which won the 2016 Postgraduate Textbook Prize awarded by the [[Royal Society of Biology]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Book Awards Winners 2016 |url=https://www.rsb.org.uk/get-involved/rsb-awards/book-awards/shortlist-2016 |website=Royal Society of Biology |accessdate=10 September 2018}}</ref>

While in graduate school, he co-authored a widely cited paper, Re-examination of the “3/4-law” of Metabolism, published in the ''Journal of Theoretical Biology''.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=P.S. Dodds |author2=D.H. Rothman |author3=J.S. Weitz |title=Re-examination of the "3/4-law" of Metabolism |journal=Journal of Theoretical Biology |date=7 March 2001 |volume=209 |issue=1 |pages=9–27 |doi=10.1006/jtbi.2000.2238|arxiv=physics/0007096 |pmid=11237567 |bibcode=2001JThBi.209....9D |s2cid=9168199 }}</ref> As a post-doctoral scholar, he published Coevolutionary arms races between bacteria and [[bacteriophage]] in the ''Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences''.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=J. S. Weitz |author2=H. Hartman |author3=S.A. Levin |title=Coevolutionary arms races between bacteria and bacteriophage |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=July 5, 2005 |volume=102 |issue=27 |pages=9535–9540 |doi=10.1073/pnas.0504062102|pmc=1172273 |pmid=15976021 |bibcode=2005PNAS..102.9535W |doi-access=free }}</ref> His notable more recent publications include Statistical structure of host–phage interactions, ''PNAS'' (2011),<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Cesar O. Flores |author2=Justin R. Meyer |author3=Sergi Valverde |author4=Lauren Farr |author5=Joshua S. Weitz| title=Statistical structure of host–phage interaction |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=July 12, 2011 |volume=108 |issue=28 |pages=E288–E297 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1101595108 |pmid=21709225 |pmc=3136311|doi-access=free }}</ref> Ocean viruses and their effects on microbial communities and biogeochemical cycles, ''F1000 Bio. Rep.'' (2012),<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Joshua S. Weitz |author2=Steven W. Wilhelm |title=Ocean viruses and their effects on microbial communities and biogeochemical cycles |journal=F1000 Biol. Rep. |date=September 5, 2012 |volume=4 |issue=17 |page=17 |doi=10.3410/B4-17|pmid=22991582 |pmc=3434959 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Viral tagging reveals discrete populations in Synechococcus viral genome sequence space, ''Nature'' (2014),<ref>{{cite journal |author=Li Deng|display-authors=etal |title=Viral tagging reveals discrete populations in Synechococcus viral genome sequence space |journal=Nature |date=11 September 2014 |volume=513 |issue=7517 |pages=242–245 |doi=10.1038/nature13459|pmid=25043051 |bibcode=2014Natur.513..242D |s2cid=4463116 }}</ref> and An oscillating [[tragedy of the commons]] in replicator dynamics with game-environment feedback, ''PNAS'' (2016).<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Joshua S. Weitz |author2=Ceyhun Eksin |author3=Keith Paarporn |author4=Sam P. Brown |author5=William C. ==Other Activities==
Weitz has published poetry, including a book of poems he wrote in college, ''Between Two Stones''.<ref>{{cite book |title=Between Two Stones: Poems |date=November 1, 2002 |publisher=Sheep Meadow |isbn=1931357021}}</ref> He has also been politically active, writing in the ''Chronicle for Higher Education'' about advocating for science,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Weitz |first1=Joshua |title=Should Scientists Compromise? First, Define Your Terms |url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/Should-Scientists-Compromise-/239402 |accessdate=10 September 2018 |work=The Chronicle for Higher Education |issue=March 10, 2017 |date=March 5, 2017}}</ref> and speaking at the Atlanta [[March for Science]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hagen |first1=Lisa |title=Thousands, Armed With Puns, March For Science In Atlanta |url=https://www.wabe.org/thousands-armed-puns-march-science-atlanta/ |accessdate=10 September 2018 |publisher=WABE |date=April 24, 2017}}</ref>
